# Meeting Brief

## Purpose

Read the supplied meeting notes and identify the purpose of the discussion. Write a concise brief for a teammate who did not attend. Use only information found in the notes and preserve the meaning of each decision. Do not invent participants, dates, agreements, or commitments.

## Decisions

Separate confirmed decisions from proposals that are still being discussed. Explain the reason for a decision when the notes provide it. Preserve conditions and disagreements that affect the outcome. If the notes contain conflicting statements, describe the conflict clearly instead of choosing a version without evidence.

## Action Items

Extract each action together with its owner and deadline when these are stated. Mark missing owners and deadlines as unspecified. Keep independent tasks separate so that a reader can track them individually. Do not turn a suggestion into an assigned task unless the notes explicitly support that interpretation.

## Open Questions

Collect unresolved questions and identify information that the team still needs. Distinguish missing information from a confirmed negative answer. Keep the wording neutral and avoid guessing what a participant intended. Include relevant dependencies so the next person can understand why a question remains open.

## Final Check

Review the brief against the original notes before returning it. Check names, dates, numbers, and the status of every decision. Remove duplicate points while retaining distinct responsibilities. Return the brief with sections for the meeting purpose, confirmed decisions, action items, and open questions.

description: Prepare a factual incident handoff from supplied observations and investigation notes.
---

# Incident Handoff

## Scope

Read the supplied incident notes and describe the affected service and the observed impact. Use facts from the notes rather than assumptions about the system. State what is known and what remains uncertain. Do not claim that a service has recovered unless the supplied evidence supports that conclusion.

## Timeline

Arrange recorded events in chronological order when timestamps are available. Preserve the original timestamps and time zones. If an event has no recorded time, identify that gap without inventing a timestamp. Separate user reports from observations made by the investigation team so their sources remain clear.

## Investigation

Summarize the checks that have already been performed and their recorded results. Distinguish a suspected cause from a verified cause. Mention evidence that contradicts a hypothesis rather than hiding it. Do not describe a proposed check as completed or infer a successful result from the absence of an error message.

## Next Actions

List the remaining investigation tasks and identify an owner when the notes name one. Explain which questions each task is intended to answer. Keep proposed mitigations separate from actions that have already been taken. Do not execute commands, modify a service, or promise a recovery time while preparing this handoff.

## Delivery

Return a concise handoff containing the current impact, timeline, completed checks, and next actions. Preserve exact error messages and technical identifiers when quoting evidence. Check that the summary contains no unsupported claims. Highlight unresolved risks so the receiving teammate can continue the investigation with the available information.

# Incident Handoff

## Scope

Read the provided incident notes and identify the service that was affected, as well as the observed impact. For events lacking a recorded time, note the absence without fabricating a timestamp. Distinguish between user reports and observations documented by the investigation team to ensure the clarity of their respective sources.

## Investigation

Summarize the checks that have been carried out and the outcomes that have been recorded. Clearly differentiate between a potential cause that is under suspicion and one that has been confirmed. Include any evidence that refutes a hypothesis rather than omitting it. Do not describe a planned check as completed or assume a successful outcome based on the lack of an error message.

## Next Actions

List any remaining investigation tasks and assign an owner if the notes specify one. For each task, clarify the specific questions it is meant to address. Separate proposed mitigations from actions that have already been completed. Do not execute commands, modify a service, or promise a recovery time while preparing this handoff.

## Delivery

Return a concise handoff that includes the current impact, timeline, completed checks, and next actions. Maintain exact error messages and technical identifiers when referencing evidence. Ensure the summary contains no unsupported claims. Clearly highlight any unresolved risks so the receiving teammate can proceed with the investigation using the available information.
